title: page-aware-reservation-and-lazy-demote-refactor
author: Maya Venkataraman
description:
Motivation: On high-concurrency tenants we've seen KV cache fragmentation and repeated paging under transient spikes. This PR introduces a page-aware reservation allocator plus lazy-demote eviction path to reduce amplification from small-object churn and paging thrash.

What this changes (summary):
- Add PageReservationManager: tracks page-granular reservations per-tenant and per-segment, enabling inexpensive fast-path allocations when contiguous slots exist.
- Replace the previous slab-centric reserve() with a page-aware fast path that tries to claim contiguous pages before falling back to existing allocators.
- Introduce LazyDemoteEvictor: when eviction pressure is encountered, frequently-accessed entries are moved to a demotion tier (soft-demoted) instead of immediate eviction; this delays paging and reduces re-fetches for short-lived spikes.
- Add a small background compaction task (compact-on-idle) that opportunistically coalesces high-fragmentation segments when CPU idle budget is available.
- Scheduler adjustments: make batch eviction runs cooperative with the continuous-batcher to avoid head-of-line latency spikes when freeing space under load.
- Kernel hints: expose an alignment hint from the allocator to selection of kernel tile sizes when sequence lengths are small (improves memory packing for attention kv caches).

Benchmarks / impact: in internal canary across 3 tenants with spiky workloads (random short-context generations + concurrent chat sessions) we saw:
- 25-40% reduction in page faulting rates during spikes
- 12% average end-to-end latency reduction at P95 for generation requests under contention
- 8% increase in sustained throughput (tokens/sec) due to fewer re-fetches

Migration notes: default behavior is opt-in via runtime config: kv.page_reservation.enabled and kv.lazy_demote.enabled. Both default to off for safety; rollout plan is canary -> 25% -> 100% across tenants.

Backwards-compatibility and safety: no on-disk format changes. All new background tasks are bounded and respect per-tenant CPU and IO budgets.

Related Linear/Jira: ENG-4528 (allocator work), ENG-4580 (eviction TTR tuning).

release_notes: Introduce page reservation allocator and lazy demotion eviction path. Opt-in via kv.page_reservation.enabled and kv.lazy_demote.enabled. Improves latency and reduces paging under spiky workloads.
discussion: Kenji Matsumoto (reviewer): The PageReservationManager looks good overall. Two concerns: how do we avoid pathological reservation monopolies by a noisy tenant? Suggest adding a soft cap and decaying lease counters.
Maya Venkataraman (author): Added per-tenant soft caps (configurable) and a decay tick in the manager. Updated docs with config knobs.
Priya Sharma (reviewer): The lazy demote metadata will add memory overhead. Can we use a compact bitset rather than full struct per-entry?
Maya Venkataraman (author): Reworked the demotion metadata to a 16-bit compact tag; used pointer packing for existing entry headers. Memory overhead reduced to ~0.6% on average in benchmarks.
Lars Holm (approver): Ran canary with 3 tenants + production-like workload. Observed reduced page faults and stable latencies. Approving with minor follow-ups in docs.
CI Bot: flaky-test-kv-compact_on_idle timed out on first run, retriggered and passed on second run.
notes_on_tests: Unit tests added for reservation fast-path, eviction demotion flow, and compact-on-idle. Integration canary config included to reproduce spike scenarios. One flaky test observed and re-run in CI.
deployment_plan: Start with internal canary (2 tenants) for 48h -> enable on 25% of production traffic with telemetry for page_faults/kvcache_evictions -> monitor for 72h -> ramp to 100% if metrics stable. Provide rollback toggle kv.page_reservation.enabled=false.
observability_changes: Added telemetry: kv.page_reservations.count, kv.page_fragmentation.score, kv.lazy_demote.promotions, kv.eviction.delay_ms. Dashboards updated with new panels in runtime/kv overview.
security_considerations: No new data paths. Per-tenant accounting ensures no cross-tenant leakage. Background compaction runs are restricted to same-tenant resource quotas.
performance_summary: Canary runs show 25-40% lower page faults during spikes, 12% lower P95 latency in contention, and ~8% throughput improvement. CPU overhead for compact-on-idle kept under 2% by default config.
follow_up: ENG-4622: auto-tune reservation thresholds from observed allocation patterns; ENG-4623: extend kernel hinting to multi-head attention kernels for further packing gains.
